seed: A motion that changes a layer's COLOUR has two colours to choose, From and To, and they used to be the only two colours in the panel that opened the Mac's own colour window: no shades, no colours out of the document, and none of the colours you had saved. This walk saves a colour called Brand off a shape's Fill, adds a Colour motion to that shape, then drives both wells. From is driven through the app's own picker, which is the proof on its own: a walk can press the app's picker and cannot touch the system colour panel at all. To is driven through the saved colours mark beside the well, by name. Both rows say the colour they are holding out loud, so each pick is read straight back, and one undo per pick puts it back.

steps.note: the shape is crimson and that crimson is saved as Brand, so there is a saved colour for the motion rows to offer
a Colour motion, starting where the layer already is. Both ends are the app's own swatch now, not the system colour well that used to sit here.

THE TEST: the From well opens the one picker every other colour row opens. A walk can see and press the app's own picker and cannot touch the system colour panel at all, so pressing a swatch inside this one is the whole proof.
the blue typed into the picker landed on From, and the row says so
THE TEST: beside the To well sits the same swatchpalette mark every other colour row wears, with Brand on it by name. Not offering the saved colours here was the whole complaint.
To is the saved crimson, and the row's summary reads the pair back: blue to crimson
one undo per pick: choosing a colour is one step, not one step per frame of the slider
and the one before it puts From back, so both picks were a single step each
